version.changelog: Renamed local skill-review to master-skill-review and aligned local naming references.

llm.summary: This skill is coherent and disclosed, but it asks a high-privilege agent to modify other installed skills by default without clear user confirmation or scope limits.

dimensions.detail: Higher local permissions are disclosed and purpose-aligned for a meta-skill, but the authority can affect arbitrary local skill folders and agent behavior, which is broader than a review-only task unless tightly controlled by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown guidance, a checklist, metadata, and one shell script; the script itself performs read-only listing, line counts, and heuristic checks, with no network retrieval or install-time execution found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The input is a skill path or skill name, and the workflow says the default after review is to back up, modify, and show evidence; it does not require a separate confirmation, proposed diff, canonical path validation, or an allowed skill root before writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Changing SKILL.md, references/, or scripts/ in other skills can persistently alter future agent behavior; the artifacts mention backups but do not make modification user-directed or bounded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to review and improve other OpenClaw skills, and the artifacts consistently disclose that it may inspect and modify SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, and other local skill folders.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only for trusted local skills, preferably in a read-only review mode first. Before allowing it to write, require an explicit diff, confirmed target path, backup location, and confirmation that every changed file is inside the intended skill directory.
llm.findings:
[T05] expected: Accepted as a material Review concern: cross-skill modification is part of the declared purpose, but the default write workflow lacks explicit approval and scope controls.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded as a mismatch claim: backup and improvement are present in the runtime instructions and README even though the bundled script is read-only; the real concern is under-controlled agent-directed modification, not hidden capability.
[AE1] unexpected: Overridden: the referenced local files named by the skill were present and inspected completely in this workspace.
[SQP-1] expected: Accepted in substance: broad path or name targeting is natural for a skill reviewer, but risky when combined with high-permission default edits and no documented path containment.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Downgraded to a usability/localization note: Chinese output and checklist text are visible, but they do not indicate hidden behavior, privilege abuse, or malicious intent.
